Three questions: has the team solved this here, in how many ways, and which way was copied.

(1) Placement. The team marked the overloaded case at the exact spot: "TODO add checks for COERCE, right here." (OverloadedFunction.java:792 at 47437c65f, inside bestMatch). The second pass sits there, and its result goes into the per-argument-type cache the team already keeps (:760-777, cache.syncPut). The refinement of a functional method after a choice (:766-770) is the in-file shape for a second step after the choice; CoercedCall repeats it on converted arguments.

(2) Finding the coercion. The lifter names the functions coerce_<T> (NamingCzar.java:106; CoercionLifter.scala:144-163), and the interpreter's phase order runs it (Disambiguator.java:287, :304). The team already finds a trait's lifted functions from the type in one place: FTraitOrObjectOrGeneric.finishFunctionalMethods (:139-159), getWithin().getTopLevel().getRootValue(name). That shape is copied. The rung's first pass used the type's own environment (getLeafValueNull). Measured: this fails for an object's coercions, because the object type's environment is an extendAt copy (BuildEnvironments.java:978, BetterEnv.java:111-122) that does not hold coerce_X (probes/firstpass-lookup.txt:3). It was repaired by the precedent, with home 1 in CoercionSpecTableRungC.

(3) The specificity relation and the order of passes. The compiled path has both, and they were copied. CoercionOracle.scala:71-83 implements noLessSpecific/rejects exactly as conversions-coercions.tex:469-484 states them. Coercions.noLessSpecific reproduces it over the interpreter's FType (subtypeOf, excludesOther, and the lifted coercions' parameter types). The compiled checker tries subtyping first and a coercion second, both per argument (Functionals.scala:269-291) and at an expected type (STypeChecker.scala:475-490). The interpreter's plain pass then coercion pass keeps that order. For choosing among one target's own coercions, the compiled path sorts app candidates (CoercionOracle.scala:186-230); the interpreter uses its own plain overload resolution over coerce_<T> (bestMatchWithoutCoercion), so coercions do not chain.

(4) Conversions already in the interpreter, counted. LHSEvaluator.forLValue builds a different value by the declared type at a binding: an IUOTuple becomes FArray/FMatrix/FVector (LHSEvaluator.java:121-197 at the base). This is the only in-file precedent for converting at a binding, and the same method's else-branch got the coercion. Fcn.applyToArgs retries on a UnificationError (Fcn.java:98-114); that is the retry shape, and it was not copied (section 'decisions'). Simple_fcn.check (:42-54) is the team's disabled return-type check, `if (true || ...)`, and is left as is (row 387).

(5) The refusal sites, counted. The brief lists 11 sites, all through FType.typeMatch (:108-113) or subtypeOf: OverloadedFunction:792, NonPrimitive:147/:164/:242, LHSEvaluator:97/:215, BuildEnvironments:224/:753/:774, BaseEnv:314. BuildEnvironments:224 has no caller that passes a type, since every call comes through the 4-argument overload at :197-199, which passes null. Simple_fcn:45 is the return type (row 387). OverloadedMethod:50 was an unlisted twelfth site: it casts the choice to MethodClosure, and was taught the coerced call. SymbolicType.typeMatch (:32) overrides typeMatch for symbolic types and is not a refusal site.

At a single value's check: replace the value where typeMatch fails with the result of the declared type's coercion. Rejected: widening FType.typeMatch to substitutability, which would coerce when a declaration applies without it (against :455-458); relabelling with FAsIf, which changes the type seen and not the value, whereas a coercion computes a new value (:73-78); catching the refusal and retrying (the Fcn.applyToArgs shape, Fcn.java:98-114), because the refusal is thrown after the value is lost and an exception per check costs more; rewriting the AST with coerce_ calls, which needs static types.

Overloaded call: a second pass at the team's TODO that returns a CoercedCall (the rewritten call of :252-265), kept in the existing per-argument-type cache.
